steps: Learn the key vocabulary for TV programmes, film genres and streaming
Master the perfect tense with avoir to talk about films you have watched
Use opinion phrases with adjective agreement to give your views
Build sentences combining past experiences with opinions and comparatives
method_card.title: TV, Film and Streaming
method_card.content:
This lesson covers TV and film vocabulary, streaming habits, and how to use the perfect tense with avoir and opinion phrases in the context of media.

FrenchEnglish
un film d'actionan action film
une comédiea comedy
un film d'horreura horror film
un film de science-fictiona science-fiction film
un documentairea documentary
une sériea series
une émissiona programme
la chaînethe TV channel
regarder en streamingto watch by streaming
téléchargerto download
le dessin animéthe cartoon / animated film
le journal téléviséthe TV news
un acteur / une actricean actor / an actress
passionnant(e)exciting / gripping
ennuyeux / ennuyeuseboring

Perfect tense with avoir: For most verbs, use avoir + past participle. The past participle of regular -er verbs ends in -é: regarder → regardé. Irregular: voir → vu, lire → lu, prendre → pris. Example: J'ai regardé une série ce soir. (I watched a series this evening.) Nous avons vu un film d'action. (We watched an action film.)

Opinion phrases: Je pense que c'est / c'était + adjective. Remember adjectives must agree: un film ennuyeux (m sg) but une émission ennuyeuse (f sg). Je trouve que + sentence. À mon avis = in my opinion.

Model paragraph: Hier soir, j'ai regardé une série policière en streaming. C'était très passionnant et les acteurs étaient excellents. Je préfère regarder des films d'action parce qu'ils sont plus excitants que les documentaires. (Last night I watched a crime series on streaming. It was very exciting and the actors were excellent. I prefer watching action films because they are more exciting than documentaries.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — media and technology appears across all papers

steps.label: Break it down
steps.content: Hier soir | j'ai regardé | un film d'action | avec mon frère | C'était très passionnant.

steps.label: Identify the tenses
steps.content: j'ai regardé = I watched (perfect tense: avoir + past participle regardé). C'était = It was (imperfect — used for descriptions in the past).

steps.label: Translate the key items
steps.content: un film d'action = an action film. passionnant = exciting / gripping. No adjective agreement needed here as it follows c'était and is masculine singular by default.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Last night, I watched an action film with my brother. It was very exciting.

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'Hier soir, j'ai regardé un film d'action avec mon frère. C'était très passionnant.'

steps.label: Check the noun's gender
steps.content: Find the noun you are describing. Is it masculine or feminine? Un film = masculine. Une émission = feminine.

steps.label: Apply the agreement rule
steps.content: Adjectives ending in -eux change to -euse in the feminine: ennuyeux → ennuyeuse. So: un film ennuyeux (m) but une émission ennuyeuse (f).

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Always match the adjective ending to the gender of the noun. Ce film est ennuyeux. (m) — Cette série est ennuyeuse. (f)

worked_examples.question: How do you make adjectives agree with feminine nouns? Give an example using 'ennuyeux'.

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for music genres, instruments and concerts
Master comparatives (plus / moins ... que) to compare music styles
Use depuis + present tense to say how long you have been doing something
Build extended sentences combining opinions, comparatives and time expressions
method_card.title: Music and Listening Habits
method_card.content:
This lesson covers music vocabulary, listening habits and how to talk about concerts, using comparatives and the depuis + present tense construction.

FrenchEnglish
la musiquemusic
écouter de la musiqueto listen to music
un chanteur / une chanteusea singer (male/female)
un groupea band
une chansona song
un concerta concert
un instrumentan instrument
jouer de la guitareto play the guitar
jouer du pianoto play the piano
le pop / le rock / le rappop / rock / rap
le jazz / le classiquejazz / classical
télécharger une chansonto download a song
talentueux / talentueusetalented
bruyant(e)noisy / loud
émouvant(e) (Higher)moving / touching

Comparatives: plus + adjective + que = more ... than; moins + adjective + que = less ... than; aussi + adjective + que = as ... as. Adjective still agrees with the noun it describes: Le rock est plus bruyant que le jazz. (Rock is louder than jazz.) La pop est aussi populaire que le rap. (Pop is as popular as rap.)

Depuis + present tense: Use depuis + the present tense to say how long something has been going on (and still is): Je joue de la guitare depuis trois ans. (I have been playing the guitar for three years.) Note: in English this uses a past tense, but in French the present tense is used.

Model paragraph: J'écoute de la musique depuis des années. Je préfère le pop parce qu'il est plus accessible que le jazz. Mon groupe préféré est très talentueux et leurs chansons sont émouvantes. (I have been listening to music for years. I prefer pop because it is more accessible than jazz. My favourite band is very talented and their songs are moving.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — music and entertainment appear across all papers

wrong.aussi: aussi means 'as ... as'. The sentence is comparing unequals, so use plus.
wrong.moins: moins means 'less'. The sentence says rock is louder (plus bruyant) than jazz, not less noisy.

gaps.correct_explain: plus starts the 'more than' comparative: plus + adjective + que.

wrong.de: de is a preposition (of/from), not used in comparatives. Use que for 'than'.
wrong.qu': qu' is used before a vowel or silent h — use que before the consonant le.

gaps.correct_explain: que completes the comparative: plus bruyant que = louder than.

wrong.jouait: jouait is the imperfect (he used to play). Depuis + present shows the action is still ongoing: joue.
wrong.a jou\u00e9: a joué is the perfect tense (he played). With depuis for an action still continuing, use the present: joue.

gaps.correct_explain: joue is the il/elle form of jouer in the present tense. With depuis, French uses the present, not the past, even when English uses 'has been playing'.

wrong.pendant: pendant means 'for' with a completed action in the past. Depuis is used with the present for actions still going on.

gaps.correct_explain: depuis means 'for' or 'since' when an action started in the past and continues now.

bronze.question: What does 'J'écoute de la musique depuis cinq ans' mean?

misconceptions.message: You picked the past tense because 'depuis' looks like it should refer to something finished. Actually 'depuis' with a present tense verb means an action still going on, so it means 'have been listening'.
You went for future tense, maybe reading 'cinq ans' as a plan ahead. But 'j'écoute' is present tense, and with 'depuis' it describes something started in the past and still happening now.
You chose 'used to listen', treating this like a habit that's stopped. In fact 'depuis' plus a present tense verb shows the action is still continuing, so it's 'have been listening'.

options: Cette chanson est moins intéressante que celle-là.

bronze.question: Which sentence correctly says 'This song is less interesting than that one'?

misconceptions.message: You picked 'plus intéressante', which actually means more interesting, the opposite meaning. For 'less interesting' you need 'moins', not 'plus'.
You chose the version with 'intéressant', forgetting that 'chanson' is feminine. The adjective needs to agree, so it must be 'intéressante' with an extra e.
You picked 'aussi... que', which means 'as interesting as', not 'less interesting than'. For a comparison showing lesser degree, you need 'moins... que'.

method_card.title: Social Media and Online Life
method_card.content:
This lesson covers social media vocabulary, daily online habits and how to give a balanced opinion using relative pronouns (qui/que) and modal verbs.

FrenchEnglish
les réseaux sociauxsocial media / social networks
partagerto share
publier / posterto post / to publish
suivre (quelqu'un)to follow (someone)
un(e) abonné(e)a subscriber / follower
un(e) influenceur / influenceusean influencer
le portable / le smartphonethe mobile phone / smartphone
l'ordinateur (m)the computer
la tablettethe tablet
utileuseful
dangereux / dangereusedangerous
le harcèlement en ligne (Higher)online bullying / cyberbullying
anonyme (Higher)anonymous
virtuel(le) (Higher)virtual

Relative pronouns qui and que: qui replaces the subject of the relative clause (the thing or person doing the action) — it is followed by a verb: C'est un réseau social qui est très populaire. (It is a social network that is very popular.) que (or qu' before a vowel) replaces the object — it is followed by a subject + verb: Le post qu'il a partagé était amusant. (The post that he shared was funny.)

Modal verbs: pouvoir (can), devoir (must), vouloir (to want). They are followed by an infinitive: On peut partager des photos. (You can share photos.) On doit faire attention en ligne. (You must be careful online.) Je veux suivre cet influenceur. (I want to follow this influencer.)

Model paragraph: J'utilise les réseaux sociaux tous les jours. C'est pratique parce qu'on peut communiquer avec des amis qui habitent loin. Cependant, je pense qu'on doit faire attention aux informations qu'on partage en ligne. (I use social media every day. It is practical because you can communicate with friends who live far away. However, I think you must be careful about the information you share online.)

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for video games, consoles and online gaming

Use time markers to describe your digital habits
Give balanced opinions about gaming using opinion phrases and comparatives
method_card.title: Gaming and Digital Entertainment
method_card.content:
This lesson covers video game vocabulary, online gaming habits and how to talk about screen time using depuis + present tense and time markers.

FrenchEnglish
le jeu vidéo / les jeux vidéothe video game / video games
le jeu en lignethe online game
jouer en ligneto play online
la consolethe console
l'ordinateur (m)the computer
le smartphone / le portablethe smartphone / mobile phone
un joueur / une joueusea player (male/female)
le niveauthe level
gagner / perdreto win / to lose
un écrana screen
virtuel(le)virtual
passer du temps (à + infinitive)to spend time (doing something)
il faut un équilibreyou need a balance
la dépendance (Higher)addiction / dependency
anonyme (Higher)anonymous

Depuis + present tense: Use depuis + the present tense to say how long you have been doing something that is still going on: Je joue aux jeux vidéo depuis cinq ans. (I have been playing video games for five years.) Elle joue en ligne depuis une heure. (She has been playing online for an hour.)

Time markers: tous les jours (every day), le soir (in the evening), le week-end (at the weekend), pendant deux heures (for two hours), après les cours (after school), depuis longtemps (for a long time).

Balanced opinions: D'un côté ... de l'autre côté ... (On one hand ... on the other hand ...). C'est utile parce que ... / C'est dangereux si ... / Il faut un équilibre. Use neutral language: facts, opinions, a conclusion.

Model paragraph: Je joue aux jeux vidéo depuis trois ans. Je joue en ligne le week-end, pendant environ deux heures. C'est amusant et on peut jouer avec des amis. Cependant, il faut un équilibre — on ne doit pas passer trop de temps devant un écran. (I have been playing video games for three years. I play online at the weekend, for about two hours. It is fun and you can play with friends. However, you need a balance — you should not spend too much time in front of a screen.)

bronze.question: What does 'Je joue aux jeux vidéo depuis six mois' mean?

misconceptions.message: You picked this because depuis looks like it could mean 'ago', matching il y a. But depuis with present tense means an action started in the past and continues now: 'have been playing'.
You picked this thinking joue looks forward, but joue is present tense here. Depuis with a present tense verb describes something ongoing from the past to now, not something planned.
You picked this assuming depuis works like passé composé, showing a finished action. Actually the present tense plus depuis shows the gaming is still happening now, not stopped.

Il faut un équilibre entre les jeux vidéos et les autres activités.
bronze.question: Which sentence correctly says 'You need a balance between gaming and other activities'?

misconceptions.message: You picked this because many nouns ending in -e take une, but équilibre is actually masculine, so it needs un, not une.
You picked this using des for 'some', but here 'other activities' and 'video games' are general categories, so French needs the definite article les, not des.
You picked this pluralising vidéo to match jeux, but vidéo is invariable when used adjectivally with jeux, so it stays jeux vidéo with no extra s.
